rows.citation: Goaillard J-M, Marder E (2021). Ion Channel Degeneracy, Variability, and Covariation in Neuron and Circuit Resilience. Annual Review of Neuroscience, 44, 335-357.
rows.model_type: biological neurons and circuits; conductance-based modelling discussed conceptually (review)
rows.controlled_mutations: no; reviews biological conductance variability and experimental deletions/pharmacology, not recorded single-fault model mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear; abstract notes perturbations and pharmacological manipulations reveal differences; full text not accessed (no open copy found).
rows.electrophysiology_features: unclear; discusses intrinsic properties and similar behaviour conceptually; no feature-extraction pipeline evident from abstract.
rows.protocol_optimization: no; no stimulus or test selection method described in abstract.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; narrative review without a model-testing evaluation design.
rows.ai_transformations: no; no AI or code transformations involved.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Biological rationale only: degenerate conductance sets look alike yet respond differently to perturbation. NeuroSem would operationalise this as automated multi-protocol regression testing of edited models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (title, authors, vol 44, pp 335-357, 2021, abstract); Europe PMC core record PMID 33770451 (abstract). Full text not accessed.

rows.citation: Korngreen A (2026). Neuronal excitability and parameter variability in the Hodgkin-Huxley model. PLOS Computational Biology, 22(6), e1014458.
rows.model_type: Hodgkin-Huxley squid axon cable model (multi-compartment ODE in custom Python/JAX), not NeuroML
rows.controlled_mutations: no; Monte Carlo sampling of whole parameter vectors from bootstrap/range distributions, not single recorded fault operators.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial; one ramped square current pulse shape (70 ms) at several amplitudes; no ramp, rebound or other protocol families.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial; classifies firing phenotype (non-firing, phasic, regular, spontaneous), firing rate, conduction velocity; custom spike detection, not eFEL.
rows.protocol_optimization: no; stimulus fixed a priori; Sobol sensitivity ranks parameters, not protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; single-model ensemble analysis without a discovery/held-out split.
rows.ai_transformations: no; no AI-generated edits or translations studied.
rows.software: HodgkinHuxleyVariability (custom Python, JAX, Diffrax, SALib) https://github.com/alon67/HodgkinHuxleyVariability (no license declared per GitHub API)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows parameter influence is regime- and time-dependent via global sensitivity analysis; NeuroSem instead tests discrete single-fault edits against calibrated tolerances across a selected protocol battery with held-out models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata, abstract); PLOS article page (methods: stimulus, Python/JAX/Diffrax/SALib, data availability); Europe PMC record PMID 42371975 / PMC13336477; GitHub REST API for repository.

rows.citation: Korngreen A (2026). Toward Reference-Grade neuron models. Communications Biology, 9.
rows.model_type: data-driven biophysical neuron models in general (conceptual)
rows.controlled_mutations: no; proposes provenance, uncertainty budgets and ensembles; no mutant generation.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial; argues equivalence shown on restricted protocols is weak and modules should declare stimulus ranges; no battery implemented.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial; mentions fitting to firing features and validation targets conceptually; no extraction method.
rows.protocol_optimization: no; recommends sensitivity analysis as a parameter gate, not protocol selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; position piece with no evaluation.
rows.software: none (cites SciUnit and Uncertainpy as possible tools)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Motivates why restricted-protocol equivalence is weak and why reference models need provenance; NeuroSem would provide an empirical, mutation-calibrated multi-protocol test method, which this Comment does not.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata); Europe PMC core record PMID 42342835 (type brief-report/Comment) and full text PMC13294341 (body read).

rows.citation: Gnanaraj V (2026). A Semi-Analytical Verification Framework for Pospischil-Type Cortical Neuron Models: Parameter Estimation, Independent Cross-Validation, and a Mouse-Human Comparison. Research Square (preprint, not peer reviewed).
rows.model_type: Pospischil-type regular-spiking conductance-based single-compartment model with M-current, fitted to Allen Cell Types recordings (custom Python)
rows.controlled_mutations: no; a real unit bug (factor 1000) was found incidentally via cross-solver comparison; no systematic fault injection.
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear; abstract mentions matched input current per specimen; protocol set not described in abstract or landing page.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial; uses spike count, first-spike latency and adaptation strength plus trace RMSE and correlation; eFEL not mentioned.
rows.protocol_optimization: no; optimisation targets model parameters, not stimulus protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; extends pipeline to a human specimen, but no held-out evaluation of a detection method.
rows.ai_transformations: no; no AI-generated edits studied (JIT compilation is a performance step).
rows.software: none (no code repository linked on Research Square landing page)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Detects numerical faults by independent-solver cross-checking of one model; NeuroSem would target edit-induced drift with a calibrated multi-protocol feature battery, injected mutants and held-out models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (posted-content, Research Square, abstract); Europe PMC preprint record PPR1316489; OpenAlex work record; Research Square landing page (CC BY 4.0, preprint status, no code link). Full PDF not read.
rows.found_via: Europe PMC '"neuron model" AND validation AND SRC:PPR' | Crossref bibliographic query (cross-simulator comparison neuron models NeuroML); verified via Crossref works API

rows.citation: Manninen T, Havela R, Linne M-L (2017). Reproducibility and Comparability of Computational Models for Astrocyte Calcium Excitability. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics, 11.
rows.model_type: astrocyte calcium excitability ODE models (non-neuronal, not spiking conductance-based), reimplemented in MATLAB and Python
rows.controlled_mutations: no; manual reimplementation found equation errors in two publications; no systematic mutant generation.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial; compared four models under shared stimuli/parameters and other stimulation conditions (glutamate/IP3 inputs), chosen manually.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial; compared calcium signal dynamics and percentage changes in outputs; no membrane electrophysiology features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no; stimuli taken from original publications or chosen manually.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; four-model case study without a discovery/held-out split.
rows.software: reimplemented Python models in ModelDB, accessions 223144, 223269, 223273, 223274 (https://senselab.med.yale.edu/modeldb)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Manual evidence that reimplementation silently changes behaviour and that further stimuli help expose it; NeuroSem would automate this for neuron models with mutants, calibrated tolerances and selected protocols.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata); Europe PMC core record PMID 28270761 (abstract); Europe PMC full text PMC5318440 (methods: simulations, software, ModelDB accessions).
